metadata.provenance: Current source baseline cc10290. Input benchmark baseline built before production edits. Core/allocator baselines match SHA256 of pass 05 accepted candidate; API baseline copied from pass 05 full release-test build. Final candidate 3 includes singleton validation fast path and linear lookup through eight declarations. Extended allocator baseline/candidate use identical harness and actual respective production source; driver restores candidate in finally. No concurrent builds/tests during timings.

change: Build a borrowed declaration index during duplicate-name validation for interfaces larger than eight inputs; preserve existing declaration/value/source checks and their order. Avoid uniqueness allocation for zero/singleton schemas; retain linear lookup and prior allocation footprint for small interfaces. Index stays private and ephemeral.
interpretation: Large 1000-input interfaces are scaling probes: in-process supplied parsing ~86% lower, resolution ~80%, program-argument validation ~66%. Two 120-sample fresh CLI repeats show check/run/inspect medians ~27-33% lower; up to 64 inputs remain within 1%. Single-input parsing/resolution helpers ~11-15% lower; native API JSON/no-input workloads approximately flat. These are local warm-cache macOS observations, not typical-script speedups, cold startup, other-platform timings or a Bash comparison.
tradeoffs: For 64 and 1000 inputs, the temporary index adds 880 and 14696 requested allocation bytes respectively; allocation counts unchanged. Through eight inputs allocation traffic does not increase, and singleton validation avoids one 192-byte allocation. Peak/RSS/live memory not measured. Unrelated microcontrols vary: final manifest-list validation +8.27%; earlier cron control +9.33% then -6.76% on repeat with the same binaries. All samples retained; do not attribute unchanged-code variation to wins or claim universal performance improvement.
refinement: Version 1 always-index candidate slightly increased singleton helper latency; rejected in favor of zero/singleton allocation-free path.
Version 2 indexed eight-input schemas without useful timing gains and requested 88 extra bytes; final version retains linear lookup through eight declarations.

summary.method: Serial preserved release test executables; alternating order. Each executable reports warmup and batched raw in-process samples. No concurrent builds/tests permitted. Round medians are descriptive, not a confidence interval or cold-start/OS-process measurement.

baseline-1.method: Native in-process input interface operations, includes allocations/destruction and schema validation; fixture creation, source parse, hashing excluded. 10 warmup plus 50 measured batches, batch size scales by declaration count. Exact map/type/inspection oracles checked before timing. No child processes. Large interfaces are scaling probes, not typical script speedups.

baseline-1.method: Native Rust runtime API, no child processes. Fixture construction, parsing and input hashing excluded; validation, supplied input resolution, preflight, signal registration, cwd canonicalization, pure typed JSON selection/encoding and result destruction included. Every workload verified as exact bytes 42, zero processes, zero cache hits before timing. 10 warmup batches and 50 measured batches, 10 operations per batch. Warm filesystem caches, uncontrolled background activity; not isolated input resolution or CLI latency.

cli_repeats.method: Identical source, inputs and catalog on preserved native release binaries. Fresh CLI processes, five excluded warmups per case and randomly interleaved serial samples, warm filesystem cache. Includes process startup, parse, validation, typed resolution, execution/inspection and output transport. Every output/status/stderr checked; full typed interface and zero native launches verified outside timing. No concurrent builds/tests. Large 1000-input schemas are scaling probes, not typical scripts, cold-cache results or a Bash comparison.
